title: Modulation of aggression neural networks in a VR real-time fMRI neurofeedback study
summary:
The aim of this research project is to examine how people can control brain activity that is linked to the regulation of aggressive behavior, using real‑time fMRI neurofeedback. Real‑time fMRI neurofeedback means that you lie inside an MRI scanner while we give you feedback about your brain activity. Earlier studies have shown that changing emotional states (e.g., anger or frustration) is associated with certain patterns of brain activity. In our project we want to find out whether you can learn to deliberately regulate the brain activity that is associated with cognitive control. For this, we use neurofeedback, which allows us to provide you with information about your brain activity. We want to explore whether you can use this information to learn to influence your brain activation voluntarily.  
In short, the project investigates the participants’ ability to regulate brain activation that is related to cognitive control using fMRI neurofeedback.

Specific objectives:
We want to investigate whether participants can regulate their brain activity that is linked to cognitive control.  
In addition, we want to examine how the training affects aggressive behavior and personal well‑being.
conditions: Patients with substance use disorders, psychotic disorders, affective disorders, anxiety disorders, acute anorexia nervosa, PTSD, ASPD, BPD, CD, ODD, ADHD, ASD with and without elevated aggressive behavior at study intake.
Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use
Behavioural syndromes associated with physiological disturbances and physical factors
Disorders of adult personality and behaviour
Behavioural and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence

interventions.name: Real-time fMRI Neurofeedback training: Participants receive neurofeedback from a brain region which is involved in cognitive control and emotion regulation
fMRI Yoked-neurofeedback: Participants receive feedback from a previous participant, unrelated to their own brain activity
Treatment as usual (TaU): Patients receive the usual treatment they would receive and no additional interventions

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
- psychiatric illness

healthy controls:
- no known psychiatric condition

all:
- age from 18 to 60 years old
Exclusion criteria:
Patients:
- acute neurological or somatic condition

Healthy controls:
- acute psychiatric, neurological or somatic condition

all:
- acute suicidality
- lack of ability to confirm their wish to participate in this study or inability to understand the project or give written confirmation to participate in this project 

MRI contraindications
